sources.edition: Kisari Mohan Ganguli, trans., The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, Book 5: Udyoga Parva (1883–1896), digitized text in the Internet Sacred Text Archive; sectional labels and printed page numbers follow this edition.

notes: Passage-checked war roster from Ganguli, Mahābhārata Udyoga Parva §§LVII–LVIII. Section LVII (pp. 134–136) directly names allied and Kuru-side warriors, describes the Pāṇḍava host’s intended opponent assignments, and says those named allies will fight the Dhṛtarāṣṭra host. Section LVIII (pp. 137–138) records named Kuru-side figures who do not desire war and the three figures Dhṛtarāṣṭra says are leading Duryodhana toward it.

The batch contains only individually named people. Group labels and unnamed relatives (for example, the Kekaya brothers, Draupadī’s other sons, Dhrishtaketu’s son, and Duryodhana’s brothers) are excluded.

Sātyaki and Yuyudhāna are one person because §LVII explicitly says “Satyaki, otherwise called Yuyudhana.” Sanjaya’s “mighty king of the Madras” is not merged with Śalya in opponent assignments because this passage does not explicitly equate the forms.

Reused clear IDs from existing expansion batches include Yudhiṣṭhira, Kṛṣṇa/Vāsudeva, Cekitāna, Sātyaki, Drupada, Virāṭa, Bhīṣma, Śalya, Duryodhana, Karṇa, Jayadratha, Vṛhadvala, Droṇa, Somadatta, Kṛpa, Aśvatthāman, Sañjaya, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Vidura, Sahadeva, Śakuni, Suvala, and Nakula, and the existing Mahābhārata IDs for Dhṛṣṭadyumna, Śikhaṇḍin, and Abhimanyu.
